rs_display_width.description: The width of the display in characters, corresponding to the -w option.

rs_input_delimiter.description: The single character used to delimit input columns, corresponding to the -c option.

rs_output_delimiter.description: The single character used to delimit output columns, corresponding to the -C option.

rs_output_rows.description: The desired number of rows in the output array. 0 means auto-calculate.

rs_output_cols.description: The desired number of columns in the output array. 0 means auto-calculate.

rs_gutter_percent.description: The gutter width (inter-column space) as a percentage of the maximum column width, corresponding to the -G option.

rs_skip_lines.description: The number of initial input lines to ignore, corresponding to the -k option.

rs_right_align.description: Right-adjust entries within columns, corresponding to the -j option.

rs_char_mode.description: Consider each character of input as an array entry, corresponding to the -E option.

rs_line_mode.description: Consider each line of input as an array entry, corresponding to the -e option.

rs_transpose.description: Transpose the input (fill output rows using input columns), corresponding to the -t option.

rs_print_shape.description: Print the shape of the input array and do nothing else, corresponding to the -h option.

rs_pad_nulls.description: Use null entries to pad out lines with fewer entries than the first, corresponding to the -n option.

rs_recycle_input.description: Pad the output by recycling the input from the beginning, corresponding to the -y option.

rs_shrink_widths.description: Shrink column widths to fit the largest entries, corresponding to the -z option.

rs_no_trim.description: Do not trim excess delimiters from the ends of the output array, corresponding to the -m option.
